Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

options.text: A survey found that most senior citizens now travel in private cars driven by family members, and most of them said they would switch to buses if travel were free
Bus drivers in the city are well trained
Many senior citizens enjoy walking in parks
The city plans to buy more buses next year

solution.concept: Strengthen: show that the target group will change behaviour
solution.explanation: The argument needs senior citizens who now use cars to switch to buses. The survey shows that they now use cars and would switch if the bus were free.
steps: Link needed: car users switch to buses
Survey supplies both parts
solution.why_others_wrong: Driver training, walking habits and future bus purchases do not show that car trips will be replaced.
solution.final_answer: Option A: A survey found that most senior citizens now travel in private cars driven by family members, and most of them said they would switch to buses if travel were free

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Passage: A bank branch has 1,200 savings accounts, of which 300 are dormant. Exactly one-third of the active (non-dormant) accounts have a debit card linked to them.

Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?

options.text: Exactly 400 accounts have a debit card linked to them
Exactly 300 active accounts have a debit card linked to them
No dormant account has a debit card linked to it
At most 300 accounts in the branch have a debit card linked to them

solution.concept: Compute only what the data fix
solution.explanation: Active accounts = 1,200 − 300 = 900; one-third of them is 300. The passage is silent about cards on dormant accounts, so totals for all accounts cannot be fixed.
steps: Active = 900
900 ÷ 3 = 300 active accounts with cards
Dormant accounts' cards unknown
solution.why_others_wrong: 400 takes one-third of all 1,200 accounts; the other two options make claims about dormant accounts, which the passage does not cover.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Exactly 300 active accounts have a debit card linked to them

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Statement: An inspection found that a government hospital ran short of oxygen cylinders several times this year because the supplier stopped deliveries after its bills remained unpaid for months.

Which of the following is the most appropriate course of action?

options.text: Stop admitting patients who may need oxygen
Blacklist the supplier for stopping deliveries
Clear the supplier's pending bills, pay future bills on a fixed schedule, and monitor the cylinder stock regularly
Ask patients' families to bring their own cylinders

solution.concept: Remove the root cause and prevent a repeat
solution.explanation: Deliveries stopped because of unpaid bills. Paying the dues restores supply, a payment schedule prevents a repeat, and stock monitoring catches shortages early.
steps: Cause: unpaid bills
Remedy: pay, schedule, monitor
solution.why_others_wrong: Refusing patients or burdening families is harmful; blacklisting the supplier punishes it for the hospital's own failure to pay and does not secure supply.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Clear the supplier's pending bills, pay future bills on a fixed schedule, and monitor the cylinder stock regularly

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Passage: Train A leaves a station at 7:00 am and runs at a steady 60 km/h. Train B leaves the same station at 8:00 am on a parallel track in the same direction and runs at a steady 80 km/h. Neither train stops.

Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?

options.text: Train B draws level with train A at 10:00 am
Train B never catches up with train A
Train B draws level with train A at 12:00 noon
Train B draws level with train A at 11:00 am

solution.concept: Head start ÷ relative speed
solution.explanation: At 8:00 am train A is 60 km ahead. B gains 80 − 60 = 20 km every hour, so it closes the gap in 60 ÷ 20 = 3 hours: at 11:00 am.
steps: Head start = 60 km
Relative speed = 20 km/h
solution.why_others_wrong: 10:00 am uses a 2-hour catch-up; noon adds an extra hour; B is faster, so it must catch up.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Train B draws level with train A at 11:00 am

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Argument: Pupils who eat breakfast at home score higher in tests than pupils who do not. So the school's new free-breakfast scheme will raise the test scores of the pupils who now skip breakfast.

Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?

options.text: In this school, the pupils who eat breakfast at home come mostly from families that also pay for private tuition, while those who skip breakfast mostly do not get tuition
The free breakfast will include fruit and milk
Some teachers also eat breakfast at school
The scheme will be paid for by a local trust

solution.concept: Weaken: offer another explanation for the correlation
solution.explanation: If breakfast-eaters also get private tuition, their higher scores may come from tuition rather than from breakfast. Then giving breakfast alone need not raise the others' scores.
steps: Evidence: breakfast-eaters score higher
Alternative cause: tuition
⇒ breakfast may not be what helps
solution.why_others_wrong: The menu, teachers' meals and the source of funding do not touch the link between breakfast and scores.
solution.final_answer: Option A: In this school, the pupils who eat breakfast at home come mostly from families that also pay for private tuition, while those who skip breakfast mostly do not get tuition

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Argument: A company says that its new four-day work week has made its staff more productive, because the company's weekly output has stayed the same although working hours fell by a fifth.

Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

options.text: Most employees said they liked the four-day week
The company measured weekly output in the same way before and after the change, and it did not add staff or machines during that period
Other companies in the city still work five days a week
The company's office is close to a metro station

solution.concept: Strengthen: rule out other explanations for steady output
solution.explanation: Same output from fewer hours means more output per hour only if nothing else changed. Ruling out new staff, new machines and a change in how output is measured supports the claim.
steps: Claim: output per hour rose
Strengthener: no other change could explain steady output
solution.why_others_wrong: Liking the new week, other firms' schedules and the office's location do not bear on output per hour.
solution.final_answer: Option B: The company measured weekly output in the same way before and after the change, and it did not add staff or machines during that period

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Argument: District X has more road accidents every year than any other district of the state. This shows that drivers in District X are the most careless in the state.

Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?

options.text: District X has the state's largest bus depot
Most accidents in District X happen at night
District X has by far the most vehicles and the longest road network in the state, and its accidents per 10,000 vehicles are below the state average
District X's traffic police were given new uniforms last year

solution.concept: Weaken: totals versus rates
solution.explanation: A larger number of accidents may simply reflect far more vehicles and roads. If the accident rate per vehicle is below the state average, X's drivers are, if anything, less accident-prone than average.
steps: Evidence: highest total accidents
Weakener: highest exposure, below-average rate
⇒ totals do not show carelessness
solution.why_others_wrong: A bus depot, night-time accidents and new uniforms do not compare the care taken by drivers across districts.
solution.final_answer: Option C: District X has by far the most vehicles and the longest road network in the state, and its accidents per 10,000 vehicles are below the state average

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Passage: A bank's gross NPA ratio is its gross non-performing assets divided by its total loans. Over the last year, Bank Y's gross non-performing assets fell by 10%, while its total loans grew by 10%.

Which of the following must be true?

options.text: Bank Y's gross NPA ratio fell by exactly 10%
Bank Y's net profit rose during the year
Bank Y wrote off some of its bad loans during the year
Bank Y's gross NPA ratio fell during the year

solution.concept: Ratio = numerator ÷ denominator
solution.explanation: The numerator was multiplied by 0.9 and the denominator by 1.1, so the ratio became 0.9 ÷ 1.1 ≈ 0.82 of its old value — a fall of about 18%. It certainly fell, but not by exactly 10%. Profit and write-offs are not covered.
steps: New ratio = old × 0.9 ÷ 1.1 ≈ 0.82 × old
⇒ the ratio fell (by about 18%)
Profit and write-offs: no information
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Exactly 10%' ignores the growth in loans; profit and write-offs are not given in the passage.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Bank Y's gross NPA ratio fell during the year
